section_1.title: The Intuition: When Transformations act as Scaling
section_1.content: Introduce the concept that most vectors change direction when multiplied by a matrix. Define 'Eigenvectors' as the special vectors that only change in length (scale), not direction. Visualize a grid being sheared and identify the single line of vectors that stays fixed in its span.
section_1.example: Imagine a rubber sheet being stretched. Most ink marks on the sheet move diagonally, but a line drawn along the direction of the stretch stays perfectly aligned.

section_2.title: Formal Definition: Av = λv
section_2.content: Break down the fundamental equation: A (matrix) * v (eigenvector) = λ (eigenvalue) * v. Explain that λ represents the 'scaling factor'. If λ > 1, the vector stretches; if 0 < λ < 1, it shrinks; if negative, it flips direction.
section_2.example: If matrix A represents a transformation, and v = [1, 1] results in A[1, 1] = [2, 2], then the eigenvalue λ is 2.

section_3.title: Finding Eigenbasis: A New Perspective
section_3.content: Define 'Eigenbasis' as a set of eigenvectors that act as a new coordinate system. Explain that when we use these as our basis, the matrix A becomes a simple 'Diagonal Matrix', making complex computations trivial.
section_3.example: Think of a complex gear system (matrix A). If you view it from the perspective of the axles (eigenbasis), the motion is just simple rotation, not a tangled mess of gears.

section_4.title: Application: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
section_4.content: Briefly connect the theory to real-world data science. Explain that finding the 'eigenbasis' of a dataset allows us to see the 'directions of maximum variance'.
section_4.example: A smart camera tracking a dog running: The camera uses eigenvectors to determine the primary axis of movement, ignoring minor shakes and focusing on the path of the animal.

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.9
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
